Assume that $f\in \SS^2(\TT;V^\star)$. Then,
    the estimator is reliable and efficient in the sense

issues.failure_explanation: The scheme in eq:cnscheme requires the point value f(t_{T+1}) (second equation), and the error estimator requires ∂_t f to exist as an L²(T;V*) function. Neither is guaranteed by the standing assumption f ∈ L²(0,t_end;V*). Lemma lem:reliability explicitly assumes f ∈ S²(Τ;V*) for the efficiency estimate, but Theorem thm:optimal_timestepping does not state this or any equivalent condition. For general f ∈ L², the scheme and estimator are not even well-defined, so the theorem as stated has no content.

failure_location.quote: Let $V$ be finite dimensional and let the initial mesh $\TT_0$ be uniform. Moreover, let the marking parameter $0<\theta\leq 1$ be sufficiently small, and let the grading parameter $G\in\N$ be sufficiently large.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis f ∈ S²(Τ;V*) (piecewise quadratic in time with values in V*) — or an equivalent condition guaranteeing well-defined point values and an L² derivative — to Theorem thm:optimal_timestepping and to the surrounding framework, matching the assumption already used in Lemma lem:reliability.
issues.overall_effect: The main optimality theorem thm:optimal_timestepping and all MOR results that invoke it (eq:convergence_time_approx_V_rb_R, thm:exp_conv, thm:fully_discrete_error) are stated without sufficient hypotheses on f to make the time-stepping scheme and error estimator well-defined. For general f ∈ L² the algorithm cannot even be executed.
issues.title: Missing regularity hypotheses on f for scheme well-definedness and estimator
issues.why_classification: The fix is to state a hypothesis the proofs already require (f ∈ S²(Τ;V*)), preserving the method, rate, and guarantees for the class of problems the framework can handle. However, this is not a purely local edit: it restricts the stated scope from all f ∈ L² to piecewise polynomial f, a substantive narrowing of the theorem's quantifiers that must be propagated to all dependent results.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the linear part ${\rm Lin}_{\II_i}:=\set{q\in \PP^1(\II_i;\R)}{q(t_T)=0\text{ for all }T\in\II_i}$,
Let $u\in \SS^2(\II_i;\R)$ with $u=u_{\rm F}+u_{\rm Quad}+u_{\rm Lin} \in {\rm F}_{\II_i} + {\rm Quad}_{\II_i} + {\rm Lin}_{\II_i}$ for an arbitrary region $\II_i$.

issues.failure_explanation: For a region Ι_i with n ≥ 2 elements, the space Lin_{Ι_i} of globally linear functions vanishing at all left-endpoint mesh points t_T is {0} (a linear function with n ≥ 2 distinct zeros must vanish). The element-wise invisible quadratics q_T satisfy q_T(t_T) = 1 and are only defined on T, so their sum Σ c_T q_T is discontinuous and not in S²(Ι_i). Hence dim(F_{Ι_i} + Quad_{Ι_i} + Lin_{Ι_i}) ≤ n + 0 + n = 2n < 2n+1 = dim S²(Ι_i), so the claimed decomposition of every u ∈ S²(Ι_i) is impossible. The hypothesis of Lemma lem:infsup0_lambda is therefore unfulfillable for most u, making it vacuous.

failure_location.quote: we decompose any function $u\in \SS^2(\TT,\R)$ into three parts, i.e., $u=u_{\rm F}+u_{\rm Quad}+u_{\rm Lin}\in {\rm F}_{\II_i} + {\rm Quad}_{\II_i} + {\rm Lin}_{\II_i}$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redefine F_{Ι_i}, Quad_{Ι_i}, and Lin_{Ι_i} as element-wise (possibly discontinuous) subspaces so that on each element T the restriction u|_T decomposes as c_T q_T + (visible part), and adjust the statements of Lemmas lem:infsup0_lambda–lem:infsup2_lambda accordingly. The proofs already work element-wise and would survive with minor rephrasing.
issues.overall_effect: The entire inf-sup stability argument (Lemmas lem:infsup0_lambda through lem:infsup_lambda, Theorem thm:infsup) rests on a decomposition that does not exist. This in turn undermines the Céa estimate, non-degeneracy, reliability/discrete-reliability, and all downstream optimality and MOR results. The element-wise analysis in the proofs can be salvaged, but the global decomposition as stated is false.
issues.title: Decomposition of S² into F + Quad + Lin does not hold for multi-element regions
issues.why_classification: The decomposition is mathematically false as stated (dimension count fails), but the proof strategy works with a correct element-wise decomposition. The repair requires redefining three subspaces and adjusting the statements of several lemmas, without needing new global proof architecture or losing any substantive conclusion.

issues.failure_explanation: On each non-refined element T ∈ Τ̂ ∩ Τ, inverse estimates give |η_{Τ̂}(T) − η_Τ(T)| ≤ |T|‖∂_t²(u_Τ − u_{Τ̂}) + A∂_t(u_Τ − u_{Τ̂})‖_{L²(T,V*)} ≲ ‖u_{Τ̂} − u_Τ‖_{Χ(T)}, a first-power bound. By the reverse triangle inequality in ℓ², |(Ση²_{Τ̂})^{1/2} − (Ση²_Τ)^{1/2}| ≤ (Σ|η_{Τ̂} − η_Τ|²)^{1/2} ≲ ‖u_{Τ̂} − u_Τ‖_Χ (first power). The stated bound with ‖u_{Τ̂} − u_Τ‖²_Χ (second power) is strictly stronger and cannot hold with a constant independent of the error: for small errors the left side is Θ(‖u_{Τ̂} − u_Τ‖_Χ) while the right side is Θ(‖u_{Τ̂} − u_Τ‖²_Χ), so no uniform C exists. The analogous argument claimed in the proof establishes only the first-power bound.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace ‖u_{Τ̂} − u_Τ‖²_Χ by ‖u_{Τ̂} − u_Τ‖_Χ on the right-hand side of eq:stab, matching the first-power bound that the analogous inverse-estimate argument actually proves and that the optimality framework requires.
issues.overall_effect: Lemma lem:stab_red as stated is false. The optimality proof in Theorem thm:optimal_timestepping invokes this lemma as satisfying a requirement from [infsup]; with the second-power bound the requirement is not met as claimed. The correct first-power stability estimate is standard and suffices for the optimality argument, so the downstream results survive after the correction.
issues.title: Stability estimate in Lemma lem:stab_red states wrong power of the error norm
issues.why_classification: The fix is a one-exponent local correction in the statement of eq:stab. The correct (first-power) estimate is what the standard optimality framework uses, so the method, conclusion, rate, and scope are all preserved with no new lemma or argument.
